findings.description: Run 25231306951 (policy-check on PR #84) did not actually execute the `pip install --require-hashes` path in the 'Ensure caller-data dependencies' step because the ubuntu-24.04 runner had `yaml` and `jsonschema` pre-importable (the `if ! python3 -c 'import yaml'` guard was taken). The hash-pinned install path was exercised in run 25231306964 (workflow-selftest fixture-pass-policy-check sub-run), where the packages were absent from the runner environment. This is the expected conditional-guard behavior documented in the release notes, but the primary policy-check CI run does not contain a direct execution trace of the `--require-hashes` flag.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Document in the R1 review that hash-pinned install execution evidence is from run 25231306964 (workflow-selftest), not 25231306951 (policy-check). Future CI hardening could consider a smoke-test step that runs the install in a fresh venv to guarantee hash-pinned execution on every PR regardless of runner image state.
findings.rationale: The conditional guard is correct and intentional (avoid false-fail on hash mismatch when no install runs). The CI evidence adequately covers the install path via the selftest run. This is an observability nit, not a correctness defect.

The core supply-chain hardening is correct: all five install sites properly converted to pip install --require-hashes; every package hash in requirements/policy-check.txt verified against live PyPI data (pyyaml 53/53, jsonschema 2/2, attrs 2/2, jsonschema-specifications 2/2, referencing 2/2, rpds-py 115-coverage spot-checked); transitive dependency versions are correct for jsonschema==4.23.0's declared requirements; top-level pins match pre-020M inline versions exactly; both workflow files correctly handle the SCP_RUNTIME_ROOT path vs bare path distinction; the release-gate.yml stale TF-020H3rg-002 comment is cleanly replaced; version-manifest.json bump is correct.
